newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach orders buses for next year.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach orders buses for next year.

text.p: British transport group Stagecoach Holdings Plc said on Monday it ordered 625 buses for 1997 and secured options on another 250, primarily from UK manufacturing plants owned by Sweden's AB Volvo.
The company, which currently operates a UK fleet of 7,000 vehicles, said all the buses and the options formed part of its 1997 order and the options were at pre-agreed prices.

"We remain convinced that the introduction of new vehicles provides a significant cost advantage as well as providing a high quality attractive product for our customers," a statement quoted Stagecoach chief executive Brian Souter as saying.

Of the 625 confirmed orders, some 335 will be based on Volvo B10M chassis and another 140 on Volvo Olympian chassis. Bodies will be built by a range of British companies including Alexander, Plaxton and Northern Counties.
Only 100 of the buses, to be based on Mercedes-Benz Vario chassis, will be built outside the UK.
Stagecoach is one of the three biggest British bus companies and also operates passenger rail services.
Director Barry Hinkley told Reuters that the 250 options would be placed during 1997 among the various manufacturers according to demand.
